messages:
maria: Hey @jamal @devon seeing a sudden spike of 502s from a few hosted-api tenants. Edge logs show upstream reset after the client IP flips mid-stream (X-Forwarded-For toggling). Streaming calls fail ~30-60s into the request. Any quick ideas?

jamal: Saw the same on dashboards — error rate + p50 latency unchanged but p99 for some tenants. Sample envoy excerpt: "[upstream reset] connection termination before response headers". I can paste traces if helpful.

devon: Can you paste a small repro curl? My first guess is a transparent proxy or WAF inserting PROXY protocol / changing source IP which breaks our keepalive/connection pooling. If the client IP presented to Envoy changes mid-connection the upstream might reject or reset.

maria: Repro snippet I used: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \n  -H 'Host: hosted-api.redwood.ai' \n  --http2 https://hosted-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Works most times but if I run through partner proxy it reproduces quickly. Logs show different X-Forwarded-For on successive frames.

lina: Customer reported they rolled a WAF update last night and enabled a transparent proxy feature. That could cause PROXY proto headers to appear at L4. I can reproduce locally by acting as a proxy and inserting a PROXY v1 header before TLS; result is 502 with the same envoy message.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1484 created: Pager notified (oncall).

maria: Mitigation idea: temporarily route affected tenant traffic to a pool that accepts proxy-protocol and preserves remote IP, or ask partner to disable proxy-protocol for our frontdoor. Also increasing upstream idle/keepalive timeout might reduce immediate noise.

devon: I patched ingress canary to accept proxy protocol on the proxy-origin pool and enabled preserve_remote_ip for that backend. Rolled to 5% canary. Quick tests: sending a PROXY v1 header -> connection accepted -> request proceeds instead of resetting. Logs now show "accepted PROXY v1" then normal request flow.

jamal: After the canary rollout the 502 spike fell back to baseline in the last 10m. Still want a clean follow-up: (1) postmortem with root cause, (2) telemetry for mismatch count (PROXY header seen vs client-ip change), (3) customer coordination.

lina: I'll draft the customer-facing note and coordinate with the partner WAF team to confirm whether their default is to enable proxy protocol on upgrades. Also collecting pcap and envoy traces for the PM.

maria: Thanks — please add the trace ids to the postmortem. Once we have the partner confirmation we'll either keep the ingress setting (if they permanently will send PROXY) or revert and require them to disable it. Closing thread after the doc. :thumbsup:
